subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent-run dry-run mode that keeps tools visible but blocks execution, and what security/redaction contract should it enforce across Gateway, embedded, client-hosted, tool-search, and native-tool paths?
rationale: The capability gap is clear in source, but this changes a user-facing tool-execution safety boundary and adds a new CLI flag, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Specify the core dry-run contract first
options.body: Approve the direction only after maintainers define hook ordering, preview payload shape, redaction, client-tool behavior, Gateway/local parity, and validation requirements.

options.title: Keep scoped dry-runs only
options.body: Decline a global mode for now and continue adding command-specific previews where each owner can make side effects and redaction precise.

options.title: Fold into safe workflow modes
options.body: Use the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent-mode proposals as the canonical product design and keep this issue as input to that decision.

recommendation.title: Specify the core dry-run contract first
recommendation.body: Approve the direction only after maintainers define hook ordering, preview payload shape, redaction, client-tool behavior, Gateway/local parity, and validation requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal around agent CLI, Gateway dispatch, and tool adapter behavior points to steipete, and the remaining blocker is product/security contract ownership.
